note.question: How do indivisible goods affect respecting improvement in markets?
note.overview: The paper is axiomatic mechanism design: agents privately report preferences over indivisible goods, allocation rules are evaluated for strategy-proofness and nonbossiness, and top-trading-cycles mechanisms are shown to respect improvements. Its strategic content is incentive compatibility rather than payoff-based Nash play.

models.method: Below, we introduce generalized matching problems, allowing for (un)endowed agents and objects to be initially (un)assigned.

sources.quote: Furthermore, random versions of the YRMH- IGYT mechanism by putting different probabilities on agents’ exogenous orders preserve respecting improve­ ment in the same way that random tiebreaking does in Theorem 2 (i.e., first-order stochastic dominance holds for respecting improvement), and the YRMH-IGYT mech­ anism with random tiebreaking on the weak domain satisfies respecting improvement (by using analogous arguments as in the proof of Theorem 2).

components.label: Objective and constraints
components.explanation: For an endowed agent k and another agent i, respecting improvement requires k to weakly prefer the new allocation when k's endowed object is locally raised in i's ranking while i's comparisons among all other assignments and all other agents' preferences remain fixed.
